caption: Newanforbi v. Serrato
claims: 42 USC 1983: Fourteenth Amendment (Substantive & Procedural Due Process), First Amendment (Retaliation); Declaratory Relief
status: Serrato's Rule 26(a)(1) received Sep. 9 (Montufar; dated Sep. 8). Plaintiff's went Sep. 8, 8:59 p.m. Do not file either set. Sep. 15 Zoom CMC live. MTD Sep. 30. Dkt. 22 unsigned.
judge: Hon. Ajay S. Krishnan, U.S. Magistrate Judge (N.D. Cal.)
defendants: Captain G. Serrato, Commander, Dublin Area, California Highway Patrol (individual and official capacities)
causes: Count I — 42 U.S.C. § 1983 Damages: Fourteenth Amendment -- Substantive Due Process — Arbitrary and Conscience-Shocking Denial of Mandatory U Visa Certification Duty
Count II — 42 U.S.C. § 1983 Damages: Fourteenth Amendment -- Procedural Due Process — Deprivation Without Constitutionally Adequate Process
Count III — 42 U.S.C. § 1983 Damages: First Amendment -- Retaliation for Protected Petitioning Activity
Count IV — Declaratory Relief (28 U.S.C. §§ 2201-2202) — Declaring Denial Unconstitutional and Plaintiff's Entitlement to Certification
key_facts: On November 1, 2024, CHP Officers Santiago Meza-Gonzalez (#023295) and Jose Melano (#023054) subjected Plaintiff to a false arrest based on fabricated material statements in a sworn report. CHP's own dashcam recording conclusively disproves four material fabrications: (1) false claim of 'strong distinct odor of an alcoholic beverage' — never verbalized during 62-minute encounter; (2) false characterization of speech as 'slurred' — contradicted by coherent, articulate speech throughout; (3) false claim Plaintiff 'seemed very confused and disoriented' — contradicted by Plaintiff correctly identifying his location and reading highway signs; (4) false entry of 'BEVERAGE PRESENT: YES' — only liquid found was urine in a cup. CHP itself conceded the arrest was unlawful by issuing a Penal Code §851.6 Detention Certificate on November 5, 2024, reclassifying the incident as 'a detention only, not an arrest' for 'insufficient grounds for making a criminal complaint.' The DA declined to file any charges. Officers' conduct constitutes qualifying criminal activity under 8 U.S.C. §1101(a)(15)(U)(iii): false imprisonment/unlawful criminal restraint, felonious assault/battery, perjury, and obstruction of justice/fabrication of evidence. On April 9, 2026, Plaintiff submitted a comprehensive U Visa Certification request to CHP Dublin Area with: (a) completed Form I-918, Supplement B; (b) detailed legal memorandum identifying qualifying criminal activity; (c) CHP's own POST complaint acknowledgment; (d) dashcam transcript with timestamped citations; (e) supporting exhibits. Lt. Gary Paul confirmed receipt on April 10, 2026: 'Your email has been received and your request is under review.' California Penal Code §679.10(j) requires processing within 30 days (deadline May 9, 2026). On April 20, 2026 — eleven days after receipt — Defendant Serrato issued a five-sentence boilerplate denial claiming '[a] thorough review of this incident was conducted' — demonstrably false given the complexity of the submission and simultaneous internal affairs investigation. The denial: (1) addressed no evidence whatsoever — not the dashcam, not the §851.6 Certificate, not the four documented fabrications; (2) identified no deficient statutory element; (3) applied no statutory standard; (4) failed to apply the rebuttable presumption of helpfulness under §679.10(h); (5) failed to provide specific written reasons as mandated by §679.10(g); (6) was rendered by a structurally conflicted decision-maker (Serrato as supervisor of accused officers and certifier of their crimes); (7) was issued in retaliation for Plaintiff's protected activity — filing complaints with CHP, POST, federal court, and state court.
procedural_status: §1983 action limited to the April 20, 2026 U-Visa certification denial (N.D. Cal., Oakland). ISC/ADR schedule runs through the Sep. 15, 2026 CMC. Mag. Krishnan's June 29 IFP order (complaint sufficient under §1915) has been cited as persuasive authority in Matters 1, 7, and 20. Plaintiff filed a First Amended Complaint (Doc. 10) and a concurrent Notice of Errata (Doc. 12) on Jul. 15, 2026, correcting the original Complaint's related-action disclosure (¶¶11-12) to include the Alameda Superior Court writ-of-mandate action (Case No. 26CV191136, Matter 20) it had inadvertently omitted; the errata states the amendment does not alter the FAC's factual allegations or legal theories and asks that the June 29 IFP/screening order remain in effect. USMS served Serrato Aug. 5, 2026 (Kim Schoonmaker / Office Assistant at CHP Dublin; Doc. 15 filed Aug. 6) after a Jul. 22 attempt noted 'SUBJECT DOES NOT WORK @ GIVEN ADDRESS ANYMORE.' FRCP 12 answer deadline Aug. 26, 2026. Dated service/ADR beats live in timeline.json. On Aug. 20, 2026 Plaintiff filed an Administrative Motion to Consider Whether Cases Should Be Related under Civil L.R. 3-12 and 7-11, identifying Meza-Gonzalez (3:26-cv-08271-PHK) as related; Mag. Krishnan granted that motion Aug. 24. On Aug. 26 DAG Haiyang A. Li filed Defendant's Motion to Dismiss FAC and/or Motion to Strike under Rules 12(b)(6) and 12(f) (Dkt. 18), originally noticed for Sep. 16, 2026 at 1:30 p.m. (21 days' notice; Civil L.R. 7-2(a) requires 35). Opposition original-filed Aug. 27 (page-1 stamp). Clerk's Notice (Dkt. 21, filed Aug. 28) reset the Dkt. 18 hearing to Sep. 30, 2026, 1:30 p.m., Oakland Courtroom 4, 3rd Floor, for that short-notice violation. The notice says the briefing schedule remains in effect but lists Opposition due 9/9/2025 and Reply due 9/16/2025 — those years are wrong on the face of the order; do not treat 2025 as a deadline. Notice of Supplemental Authority on the Whitman Aug. 27 tentative executed Aug. 31, unfiled — attaches the written tentative as Exhibit A. Whitman's order entered August 29, 2026, with clerk notice of entry August 31; this NSA remains unfiled and should not be filed on this record. PACER Sep. 4: Dkt. 22 is a stipulation with proposed order to continue the initial CMC (Li, Sep. 3). No order. Sep. 8 and Sep. 15 stay live. On September 7, 2026 at 9:44 p.m. Li wrote that the Court had not signed Dkt. 22 and proposed that if no order issues by 2:00 p.m. Pacific September 8, Plaintiff send his JCMS portion so the AG can file a joint statement by end of day. Reply agreeing was SENT Sep. 7 at 9:52 p.m. Do not treat the September 8 dates as vacated until a signed order is on PACER. Li filed the Joint Case Management Conference Statement on September 8, 2026 as Dkt. 24 (Plaintiff authorized /s/; Civil L.R. 5-1(i)(3) attestation). Dkt. 22 remains unsigned; the September 15 Zoom CMC and September 8 disclosure date stay live. Same day, Krishnan declined to relate Candelaria (Dkt. 23 in this action / Dkt. 13 in 3:26-cv-08272-LJC). Rule 26(a)(1) served on Li by email September 8, 2026, 8:59 p.m. Pacific (bnn.cdl@gmail.com to Haiyang.Li@doj.ca.gov, cc Andy.Marquez@doj.ca.gov): disclosures PDF plus the one-page house POS. Do not file the disclosures. Do not resend the JCMS portion. Dkt. 24 § VII.A asked Defendant to serve within seven days (Sep. 15).
damages: Compensatory damages for deprivation of meaningful access to U Visa process, causing ongoing immigration uncertainty, inability to obtain employment authorization and removal protections, severe emotional distress, anxiety, and deprivation of dignitary interest in having state actor acknowledge documented criminal misconduct by subordinate officers. Punitive damages against Serrato individually for deliberate indifference to constitutional rights, recitation of 'thorough review' unsupported by record, willful refusal to engage with evidence in own possession, and severe continuing harm caused by immigration uncertainty, loss of work authorization, emotional distress, and dignitary injury. Attorney's fees and costs under 42 U.S.C. §1988(b) and California CCP §1021.5. Pre-judgment and post-judgment interest.
risk: Favorable. No qualified immunity available — the right to non-arbitrary decision-making by state officials exercising mandatory statutory duties is clearly established (Shanks v. Dressel, 540 F.3d 1082 (9th Cir. 2008)); the right to freedom from First Amendment retaliation is clearly established (Borough of Duryea v. Guarnieri, 564 U.S. 379 (2011); Hartman v. Moore, 547 U.S. 250 (2006)). The specific statutory requirements of PC §679.10 — mandatory certification language, rebuttable presumption, specific-reasons requirement — gave Serrato fair notice that boilerplate denial ignoring evidence and statutory standards would violate constitutional rights. Structural bias claim (Serrato as supervisor and certifier) strong under Withrow v. Larkin, 421 U.S. 35, 47 (1975). Retaliation claim strong — documented knowledge of protected activity (Serrato's own March 26, 2026 acknowledgment of POST complaint and assignment of investigator), tight temporal proximity (March 23 to April 20), concrete institutional incentive (avoiding admission of officers' crimes while defending same officers in pending civil suits), and pretextual reasoning (no engagement with any evidence). Mathews v. Eldridge balancing favors Plaintiff — private interest in certification substantial; risk of erroneous deprivation extreme; governmental interest minimal.
